subject: microbiology
title: Runyon Classification, Nontuberculous Mycobacteria and Mycobacterium leprae

steps.tx: The **Runyon classification** groups nontuberculous mycobacteria by growth rate and pigment: photochromogens pigment after light, scotochromogens pigment in darkness, nonchromogens produce little pigment, and rapid growers form colonies within seven days. The scheme remains a teaching scaffold, although modern species identification uses MPT64 exclusion, line probes, MALDI mass spectrometry and gene sequencing because treatment depends on exact species.
steps.say: Runyon organises the bench, but species level identification decides modern NTM therapy.

left.title: Slow growers
points: Group I photochromogens such as M kansasii
Group II scotochromogens such as M scrofulaceum
Group III nonchromogens such as M avium complex
Colonies usually require more than seven days

right.title: Rapid growers
points: Group IV colonies within seven days
Includes M abscessus, M fortuitum and M chelonae
Often associated with water, trauma and devices
Drug patterns differ sharply by species and subspecies

steps.tx: Slit skin smears from ear lobes or lesions look for acid fast bacilli of leprosy, while pigment plates sort nontuberculous mycobacteria. The **Runyon classification** uses growth speed and colour: photochromogens colour only after light, scotochromogens colour in the dark, nonchromogens make little pigment, and colonies of rapid growers appear inside seven days. Those four groups remain a classroom map. Naming the species now uses MPT64 exclusion, probe strips, MALDI spectra or sequencing, because the drug plan needs the precise organism.

steps.tx: **Mycobacterium avium complex** includes M avium and M intracellulare and causes nodular bronchiectatic disease, fibrocavitary upper lobe disease and disseminated infection in profound cellular immunodeficiency. Environmental exposure is universal, so respiratory isolates require clinical, radiological and microbiological criteria before disease is diagnosed. Macrolide susceptibility is treatment critical, and inducible resistance can complicate long courses.
steps.say: A single sputum MAC isolate is exposure until clinical, imaging and repeat microbiology criteria agree.

left.title: Pulmonary patterns
points: Nodular bronchiectatic right middle lobe and lingula
Fibrocavitary upper lobe disease
Hypersensitivity like disease after hot tub exposure
Repeated positive cultures support true disease

right.title: Treatment principles
points: Macrolide is the cornerstone drug
Ethambutol protects against macrolide resistance
Rifamycin is commonly added
Sputum conversion and duration guide therapy length

steps.tx: **Mycobacterium kansasii** is a photochromogen that causes chronic cavitary lung disease resembling tuberculosis, especially in people with damaged lungs or immune compromise. It is usually rifampicin susceptible, a susceptibility fact with unusual importance because rifampicin based therapy is highly effective. Cross reactive tuberculin responses may occur, and molecular or culture speciation prevents a costly automatic assumption of tuberculosis.
steps.say: Kansasii can imitate tuberculosis clinically, but rifampicin susceptibility testing carries special therapeutic weight.

left.title: Clues
points: Yellow pigment after light exposure
Upper lobe cavitary disease
Tap water environmental reservoir
Dissemination in advanced immunodeficiency

right.title: Treatment
points: Rifampicin based combination when susceptible
Isoniazid and ethambutol commonly included
Macrolide substitutions in selected regimens
Treat until prolonged culture negativity

steps.tx: **Mycobacterium marinum** follows aquatic trauma from fish tanks, fishing injuries and swimming pools, producing nodular lymphangitis sometimes called **swimming pool granuloma** or fish tank granuloma. It grows better at about 30 degrees than at core body temperature, matching cooler skin. Biopsy, culture with temperature notification and molecular tests matter because lesions are paucibacillary and routine incubation can miss the organism.
steps.say: Sporotrichoid nodules after fish tank injury should trigger cooler incubation for M marinum.

left.title: Clinical pattern
points: Papule or ulcer at inoculation site
Ascending nodular lymphangitis
Hand and arm lesions predominate
Deep invasion can affect tendon and joint

right.title: Laboratory requests
points: Tell laboratory about aquatic exposure
Incubate cultures around 30 degrees Celsius
Use tissue rather than superficial swab
Consider clarithromycin and ethambutol therapy

steps.tx: **Mycobacterium ulcerans** secretes mycolactone, a cytotoxic and immunosuppressive toxin that causes **Buruli ulcer**. Early nodules evolve into painless undermined ulcers with necrotic bases, often on limbs in endemic tropical regions. Diagnosis uses IS2404 PCR from swabs or tissue, and rifampicin based oral therapy plus wound care has replaced surgery as the central approach for many lesions, though reconstruction may still be needed.
steps.say: Mycolactone makes Buruli ulcers painless, extensive and initially deceptively quiet.

left.title: Lesion evolution
points: Painless nodule, plaque or oedema
Central necrosis and undermined edge
Minimal pain despite large tissue loss
Osteomyelitis can underlie advanced ulcers

right.title: Management
points: PCR confirms when available
Rifampicin plus clarithromycin commonly used
Careful wound care and physiotherapy
Surgery reserved for debridement or reconstruction

steps.tx: **Rapidly growing mycobacteria** such as Mycobacterium abscessus complex, chelonae and fortuitum inhabit water systems and cause skin, soft tissue, surgical site, catheter and pulmonary disease. M abscessus is particularly drug resistant; the erm 41 gene can confer inducible macrolide resistance in some subspecies and must be considered. Surgical source control and susceptibility guided combination therapy often matter more than any single drug.
steps.say: Rapid growth does not mean easy treatment, especially when the species is M abscessus.

left.title: Typical settings
points: Post injection and post surgical wounds
Cosmetic procedure outbreaks
Catheter and prosthetic infections
Bronchiectasis and cystic fibrosis lungs

right.title: Treatment challenges
points: Broad intrinsic resistance
Inducible macrolide resistance possible
Amikacin and beta lactams may contribute
Removal of infected devices frequently required

steps.tx: **Mycobacterium leprae** causes leprosy, grows extremely slowly, cannot be cultured on routine artificial media, and targets skin and peripheral nerves in cooler tissues. It was propagated historically in the **mouse footpad** and can multiply in armadillos, which also serve as a zoonotic source in some regions. Slit skin smears and biopsy support classification across tuberculoid and lepromatous poles.
steps.say: Leprosy is a nerve and skin disease caused by an organism that still refuses routine artificial culture.

left.title: Microbiology
points: Weakly acid fast slender bacilli
Doubling time around twelve to fourteen days
Mouse footpad was a historic growth system
Nine banded armadillos can carry the organism

right.title: Host response spectrum
points: Tuberculoid pole has strong cellular immunity and few bacilli
Lepromatous pole has abundant bacilli and weak cellular control
Borderline states are immunologically unstable
Nerve damage drives disability more than skin signs

steps.tx: The **lepromin test** was an intradermal test using killed leprosy material. A late Mitsuda granulomatous reaction indicated strong cell mediated immunity and prognostic position toward the tuberculoid pole, not whether a person was infected. The **bacteriological index** grades bacillary density on slit skin smears, whereas morphological index estimates the fraction of solid staining, probably viable organisms and helps follow response.
steps.say: Lepromin measured host cellular response, while bacteriological index measured bacillary load.

left.title: Lepromin meaning
points: Early Fernandez reaction reflects hypersensitivity
Late Mitsuda reaction reflects granulomatous cellular immunity
Positive in tuberculoid disease and many healthy exposed people
Negative at lepromatous pole

right.title: Smear indices
points: Bacteriological index is logarithmic density grade
Morphological index is percentage solid bacilli
Sites include earlobes and lesion edges
Fite stain preserves leprosy bacilli better than harsh methods
